text:
Asha: Quick help — deployed our .NET 7 minimal API to Azure App Service and Basic auth starts returning 401 (works locally). Any guesses?

Asha: Code I'm using to build the header:
```csharp
var creds = $\"{user}:{pass}\";
var b64 = Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.Unicode.GetBytes(creds)); // yes I used Unicode here
client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue(\"Basic\", b64);
```

Matt: two quick Qs — is the same secret being read in Azure (App Setting / Key Vault) and locally? and did you paste the secret via Windows Notepad or the portal?

Asha: Same secret key name yes. Locally I'm reading from user-secrets; in Azure it's a Key Vault reference (managed identity) mounted via App Service setting. I pasted the secret into Key Vault from a Windows machine.

DevOps-bot: the App Service logs show repeated 401 from requests to downstream service (auth failing) — no inner exception in our app.

Leo: odd bit: Encoding.Unicode is UTF-16LE in .NET, not UTF-8. Many HTTP Basic implementations expect UTF-8 bytes before base64-ing. Locally the target tolerated UTF-16? also Key Vault paste could have introduced trailing CR or BOM.

Sam: can you print the raw secret bytes (hex) in a one-off log to compare local vs azure? also check for extra quotes or whitespace around the secret from Key Vault.

Asha: did a quick log (hex) and here's the diff:
- local hex starts with: 75 73 65 72 3a 70 61 73 73
- azure hex started with: 75 00 73 00 65 00 ... and ended with 0d 0a (CRLF)
So Azure value appears UTF-16 (null bytes between chars) + trailing CRLF. That matches my use of Encoding.Unicode locally when I generated the header — but when the secret in Key Vault contains raw UTF-8 it worked; the pasted value got stored as UTF-16 with CRLF.

Leo: aha. Two issues colliding: 1) the secret in Key Vault contains CRLF from the Windows clipboard, 2) you encoded using UTF-16 which will produce a different base64 than UTF-8. Downstream likely expects Basic header to be base64(utf8(\"user:pass\")).

Sam: quick fix: normalize the secret string and use UTF8 explicitly. e.g.:
```csharp
var creds = (Configuration["ApiCreds"] ?? string.Empty).Trim(); // strip CR/LF and surrounding quotes
var b64 = Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(creds));
client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Basic", b64);
```
Also add a small helper when loading secrets: Replace("\r", "").Replace("\n", "").Trim()

Asha: swapped to UTF8 + Trim() and redeployed — auth now succeeds, 200s all around. Thanks 🙏

Matt: can we add a tiny note in devex docs about normalizing secrets from Key Vault + prefer UTF8 for Basic auth? saved us an incident.

Leo: +1 — also add a unit test that base64-encodes known "user:pass" with UTF8 and asserts header string.

DevOps-bot: automated note: created ticket INF-4822 to add doc + test (assign: devex).

Asha: closing the loop — will PR the doc blurb and test later today :tada:
